fields.reasoning: cmd/rhiza/detach_unix.go already reaps each driver with go cmd.Wait() (since #210). So the 50 zombies come from the daemon re-exec'ing itself in place (internal/daemon/reexec_unix.go, syscall.Exec): the waiting goroutines die and the new image does not know the children it had. The intent's wait4(-1, WNOHANG) would cover those, but the question is right that it would also reap git/make/hook children that os/exec goroutines (some from web UI requests) are waiting on, and their Wait would fail with 'no child processes'. That is a new bug in normal operation. Detached drivers are the only children started with Setsid, so leading a session marks exactly the children the daemon itself must reap, including ones from before a re-exec. Waiting on specific pids keeps the intent's goal (no zombies, including pre-re-exec ones, with a test) and avoids the race. Running it at startup plus on a timer means a re-exec'd daemon clears its leftovers right away. The daemon runs on the Linux VM, so reading /proc is enough.
fields.statement: The daemon never calls wait4(-1). It keeps detachProgram's go cmd.Wait() for drivers started by the running image. It also adds a reaper that runs once when the daemon starts (so after every re-exec) and then on a timer. The reaper lists the daemon's own children (on Linux from /proc: ppid equal to the daemon's pid) and calls wait4(pid, WNOHANG) only on those that lead their own session (getsid(pid) == pid, i.e. a detached driver started with Setsid). Children run through os/exec for git, make and hooks are never touched, so their cmd.Wait/Output keeps working. ECHILD from a reaper/goroutine race on the same driver is ignored. Off Linux the reaper does nothing, like detach_other. The test starts a Setsid child that is not waited on, lets it exit, runs the reaper, and checks the pid is gone (no zombie), and that a plain os/exec child running at the same time still gets its own exit status.
